one_line_contribution: A transplant/difference-in-differences measurement showing that instructions produced by a reflective prompt optimizer under an injected memory bank become conditionally dependent on that specific bank (so the reported optimizer+memory gain is bank-conditional rather than a property of the instruction), plus a counterfactual-replay routing rule (CCR) that sends memory-attributable failures to the write path instead of the instruction reflector.
closest_prior_work: Two fronts. For the fix: Environment-Grounded APO for game agents (2606.17838) already runs failure attribution between a context-providing module and the agent's own prompt inside a prompt-optimization loop, and CANTANTE (2605.13295) already does contrastive trajectory-level attribution over workflow components with a prompted judge; the proposal concedes both, so CCR is an application of an existing signal to a new slot, and B9 (soft two-view) is by the authors' own account the strongest baseline precisely because it is what those papers imply. For the diagnostic, the threat is not a single paper but the standard train-regime/test-regime mismatch analysis: MIPRO/GEPA-style optimizers are known to overfit the evaluation configuration they were scored under, and Adv-ICL-style 'w/o demonstration' ablations already measure sensitivity to removing the exemplar slot. Running that same ablation on prompts optimized under two regimes is a small design increment, and the authors' rebuttal ('they ablate at evaluation time within a single optimization regime') concedes exactly how small it is. The specific arXiv item that would kill it (a transplant/DiD evaluation of optimized prompts under memory ablation) is the one query the proposal admits it never ran.
strongest_objection: The DiD in P1 is sign-ambiguous and, in the direction the authors need, close to guaranteed by construction. DiD = [R_mem@T_mem - R_mem@T_nomem] - [R_nomem@T_mem - R_nomem@T_nomem] is positive under two opposite mechanisms: (i) R_mem instructions collapse when memory is removed (co-adaptation, the paper's story), or (ii) R_nomem instructions collapse when memory is forced on them at k=7 (memory harming a prompt never written to consume it). The track's own starting position says mechanism (ii) is real and large in this exact setup: k=7 injection fixed zero items and broke six to seven. So the more likely driver of a >=5-point interaction is the baseline arm degrading, not the treated arm being brittle, and the plan never pre-registers the simple-effect decomposition that would separate them. Compounding this: the same prior result undercuts P6. If memory's in-distribution contribution at k=7 is zero or negative, then B4 memory dropout and B10 k=2 capping cost nothing at T_mem -- indeed B10 is the configuration the track already found removes the harm -- and P6's prediction that they pay >=2 points of T_mem accuracy relative to B6 fails, at which point the authors' own refutation clause fires and the method claim reduces to 'a blind regularizer would have done it.' Separately, 'co-adaptation' is not what is tested: HELD FIXED freezes Bank_A during optimization, so R_mem is unidirectional prompt overfitting to a static context, while the motivating target (ACE) has a bank that is being rewritten concurrently -- the control list even contains a 'frozen-memory ablation during R_mem optimization,' which is vacuous if the bank was frozen all along and contradicts HELD FIXED if it was not. Finally, P2's effect size is a free parameter: the T_mem->T_shift drop is set by how far the Bank_B task-family mix is pushed, there is no calibration of shift severity, and the 'drops at least twice as much' ratio is unstable because the R_nomem denominator is expected to be near zero.
what_would_fix_it: 1) Pre-register the two simple effects, not just the interaction: require acc(R_mem@T_nomem) < acc(R_nomem@T_nomem) by a stated margin as a necessary condition for reading a positive DiD as co-adaptation, and report the interaction decomposed into both arms with fix/break counts. 2) Gate the whole program on a measured memory contribution: report acc(B1)-acc(B0) at k=7 on E1 first; if it is <=0 (as the track's prior result predicts), P6 as written is dead on arrival and the B4/B10 comparison must be restated in terms of shift robustness only. 3) Make the primary R_mem arm a genuinely co-evolving one (bank edited by the write path during optimization) and demote the frozen-bank arm to the control, so the diagnostic matches the system (ACE) it claims to indict; and resolve the HELD FIXED / frozen-memory-ablation contradiction. 4) Replace the ratio form of P2 with an absolute, dose-response form: build three Bank_B variants at graded mix distance and report the drop as a function of measured shift, plus a bank-quality control (B0/B1 evaluated on each bank) so a bad bank is not read as a brittle instruction. 5) State a decision rule for the case where the interaction is large but driven by memory-referential clauses that are simply good advice under any bank -- the P3 clause analysis should be causal (ablate the memory-referential clauses from R_mem instructions and re-evaluate) rather than a 10-point Spearman correlation, which is underpowered as specified.
missing_baseline: Cheap re-optimization under the target regime. The 'rented gain' framing only bites if renting again is expensive, so a reviewer will demand: take the B3 instruction and run the same reflective optimizer for a small fraction of the budget (e.g. 100-150 rollouts) against Bank_B, then evaluate at T_shift. If a short re-optimization recovers most of the T_mem->T_shift drop at a cost far below CCR's replay overhead, P2 describes a maintenance chore rather than a failure mode, and CCR's >=3-point T_shift advantage over B3 is measured against the wrong reference. A second omission on the same axis: no condition optimizes the instruction while selecting candidates on a validation set drawn from a bank the instruction will not see at test time (regime-mixed selection over two banks), which is the obvious and nearly free robustness fix distinct from B4's within-bank dropout. Also absent: any arm where the instruction is allowed to reference the injection budget as a decision variable, despite the track's own finding that volume is the causal lever -- B10 fixes k=2 by fiat rather than letting the agent choose.
preprint_collision: The check is unusually good -- nine named items, an explicit concession that the counterfactual-replay signal is prior art (HiMPO 2606.16285, CANTANTE 2605.13295, UCOB 2606.29502), and the promotion of UCOB's idea into an explicit baseline (B9). I credit that honesty. But it fails exactly where it matters. After the concession, novelty rests entirely on the transplant/DiD diagnostic and the P2 bank-conditionality claim, and the proposal states that both search sessions were rate-limited before any targeted query on 'transplant / difference-in-differences evaluation of optimized prompts under memory ablation' could be run. So the single load-bearing novelty claim is the one item never searched, and two directly adjacent items -- 'Tracing and Attributing Errors in LLM Memory Systems' (2605.28732) and the ICLR 2026 'Counterfactual Reasoning for Retrieval-Augmented Generation' poster -- are logged as unretrieved abstracts. By the standard that an unsearched novelty claim is a weakness rather than a neutral, this is a real deduction, not a formality: a prompt-optimization robustness paper with a memory-ablation transplant table in its appendix is a plausible 2026 preprint, and the authors themselves flag it as their concentrated novelty risk. The search must be completed before this is submittable; the rest of the collision check is strong enough that finishing it is a small amount of work.
